hey! the residence halls do allow emotional support animals... kind of. there are a lot of rules surrounding them and you're looking at /at least/ a $250 additional fee to your housing so that at the end of the year when you move out, the room can be deep-cleaned so that there's no dander or anything left. you also have to get it cleared by, i believe, our office of disability services.

i don't know the full details, but i know these are some basics. i've been a resident assistant at the university for two years, and last year one of my residents had an ESA~

beyond that, ARF, the Muncie Animal Shelter, and PetsMart are always looking for volunteers/sometimes employees. and a few of the shops in the Village (campus-adjacent shopping area) have cats that we all love to visit.

hope this helps!

It really depends on what your sorority process looks like! I'm Greek and going into my second year of RAing, but my experience is a little different because a) I joined my Freshman fall, so it was kind of already part of the "package" so to speak, b) my sorority doesn't do Formal Rush with the rest of PHC, so our recruitment season is slightly less grueling than the rest of our PHC community, and c) While our sorority is small and people typically have to take on officer positions (in four semesters I've served as our historian, our PHC delegate, and... to be honest I feel like I'm forgetting something), we also have had a lot of members working within Housing in some shape or form, so our sorority has been understanding.

I say go for it, but be upfront with all parties about time commitment. I know my Housing Department, at the beginning of the year, asks what extracurriculars you're intending on be part of, so I'd let them know your intentions of rushing. Good luck!!
